report_parsed.summary: Within the authorized 300s window (2026-09-28T10:08:17Z to 10:13:17Z) the evidence does not corroborate the report of elevated checkout errors. Checkout's span-metric series carry only STATUS_CODE_UNSET (increase ~56.7 spans/5min) and no ERROR-status series was returned for checkout; every checkout PlaceOrder span in the sampled traces (trace ids a316d3abe7ebd4259d99659a8604cc76, 2db400542e073d5d42284ad1fd49632a, 42c8272f1ad39b8957e51684076553f9, 26b54e89c9da0f275c47213972db34f6, 2c7487e29ed98c74fe368c7300500efe) carries rpc.grpc.status_code 0, and the frontend /api/checkout entry spans in the sample return http.status_code 200. Dependency services cart, currency, email, product-catalog and shipping likewise show only success statuses in the returned series and in the sampled spans, and payment's app_payment_transactions_total increased ~4.4 over the window. The only error-tagged spans observed belong to payment itself (traces 94cfb05cbd9bfcebe99aa181be06f7d4 and 598acd55d2618df635fb377c26678f83, 'getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND metadata.google.internal.' and 'connect ECONNREFUSED 169.254.169.254:80'); those spans have no visible parent, so they cannot be attributed to a checkout PlaceOrder chain, and the payment STATUS_CODE_ERROR span-metric series returned an increase of 0 for span names GET, dns.lookup and tcp.connect. Absolute latency was observed (checkout server gRPC p95 ~205ms; checkout client p95 up to ~47ms for PaymentService/Charge) but no pre-window baseline is available in this run, so 'elevated' latency cannot be assessed, and the trace views are sampled, so an absence of checkout errors is not proof of a zero error rate.

claims.text: Checkout span-metric series in the window carry only STATUS_CODE_UNSET (increase 56.73 over 300s summed by status_code; per span name ~4.48-10.45). No STATUS_CODE_ERROR series for service_name=checkout was returned by either query.

Sampled checkout traces show successful PlaceOrder handling: span oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder with rpc.grpc.status_code 0 in traces a316d3abe7ebd4259d99659a8604cc76 (247008us), 2db400542e073d5d42284ad1fd49632a (74056us), 42c8272f1ad39b8957e51684076553f9 (69860us), 26b54e89c9da0f275c47213972db34f6 (60837us) and 2c7487e29ed98c74fe368c7300500efe (55949us); no checkout span in the 20 shown rows carries an error status tag.

Payment spans tagged ERROR were observed in the window: trace 94cfb05cbd9bfcebe99aa181be06f7d4 contains spans GET, tcp.connect and dns.lookup with status_tags error:true / otel.status_code ERROR and detail 'getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND metadata.google.internal.'; trace 598acd55d2618df635fb377c26678f83 contains GET and tcp.connect with ERROR and detail 'connect ECONNREFUSED 169.254.169.254:80'.

The error-tagged payment spans carry empty parent_references (parent_is_visible false / no visible parent), so no parent-child call edge from a checkout PlaceOrder span to them is evidenced; they are DNS/TCP attempts against the cloud metadata endpoint, not oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge calls.

The STATUS_CODE_ERROR span-metric series that do exist returned an increase of 0 over the window: payment span names GET, dns.lookup and tcp.connect (and payment grouped by status_code), plus frontend GET, executing api route /api/data, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, tcp.connect, frontend-proxy ingress and router frontend egress, and load-generator GET; frontend and frontend-proxy show 0 for STATUS_CODE_ERROR alongside 346.36 and 158.25 UNSET respectively.

Grouped by service and status, the window shows only UNSET status for cart (108.98), checkout (56.73), email (17.91), product-catalog (76.14) and shipping (13.44), and only STATUS_CODE_OK for currency (10.45); no error-status series was returned for any of these five dependency services or for checkout.

Checkout's own client-side view of its dependencies shows only rpc_grpc_status_code 0 calls (increase: Charge 4.47, Convert 10.42, EmptyCart 4.47, GetCart 4.47, GetProduct 5.96, GetQuote 4.47, ShipOrder 4.47), i.e. no non-zero gRPC status recorded on checkout's outbound dependency calls in this window.

Observed checkout client-call latency in the window (histogram_quantile 0.95 over increase of rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_bucket): PaymentService/Charge 47.19ms, ShippingService/GetQuote 42.55ms, CartService/EmptyCart 23.32ms, CurrencyService/Convert 9.19ms, CartService/GetCart 8.51ms, ProductCatalogService/GetProduct 4.75ms, ShippingService/ShipOrder 4.75ms. Corresponding duration sums were Charge 80.67, Convert 38.47, EmptyCart 37.76, GetCart 11.59, GetProduct 4.87, GetQuote 40.20, ShipOrder 2.60 ms.

Server-side gRPC latency series in the window were returned only for checkout (p95 205.33ms) and product-catalog (p95 4.845ms) among the seven requested services; no rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket series was returned for payment, cart, currency, shipping or email.

Every returned series in this run covers only the authorized 300s window (lookback_seconds 300 with lookback_start_at equal to the window start, e.g. 2026-09-28T10:08:17Z), so no pre-window baseline was obtained for any latency figure.

Sampled dependency spans in the window indicate successful handling with modest durations: email POST /send_order_confirmation http.status_code 200 (max 84463us in trace a316d3abe7ebd4259d99659a8604cc76), shipping oteldemo.ShippingService/GetQuote rpc.grpc.status_code 0 (max 45385us), cart POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem|GetCart|EmptyCart without error tags (max 14936us), currency Currency/Convert otel.status_code OK rpc.grpc.status_code 0 (max 2943us), product-catalog oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct|ListProducts rpc.grpc.status_code 0 (max 5610us).

app_payment_transactions_total increased 4.408 over the 300s window for the single returned series (service_name=payment, app_payment_currency=USD, job=opentelemetry-demo/payment), i.e. payment transactions were being recorded as successful activity in the window.

HTTP server request metrics in the window were returned only for cart among checkout/cart/email: http_server_request_duration_seconds_count increase 39.92 and p95 20.5ms; no http_server_request_duration_seconds series was returned for checkout or email.

Frontend entry spans for the checkout journey return HTTP 200: POST /api/checkout (69565us, trace 2c7487e29ed98c74fe368c7300500efe) and POST /api/checkout (263505us) plus grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder rpc.grpc.status_code 0 in trace a316d3abe7ebd4259d99659a8604cc76; frontend and frontend-proxy STATUS_CODE_ERROR series both read 0 for the window.

The reported 'elevated errors in checkout' may originate from the payment ERROR spans visible in this window (DNS failure resolving metadata.google.internal and ECONNREFUSED to 169.254.169.254:80), which look like cloud-metadata probe/init noise rather than checkout-order failures. This is unconfirmed: those spans have no visible parent, checkout itself shows no ERROR-status series, and the payment STATUS_CODE_ERROR span-metric series returned 0, so the relationship to the checkout journey is not evidenced.

Against any reading of the checkout data as 'no errors at all': the checkout trace view was a biased sample, returning 5 traces / 241 spans of which only 20 were shown and 221 were omitted, so error spans inside those traces (or in unsampled traces) would not necessarily appear.

Against the assumption that the payment error signals are fully captured by metrics: ERROR-tagged payment spans are present in traces during the window while the corresponding traces_span_metrics_calls_total STATUS_CODE_ERROR series for payment (GET, dns.lookup, tcp.connect and grouped by status_code) returned an increase of 0, an observed inconsistency between the two views whose cause is not established here.

'Checkout PlaceOrder calls failed or returned errors during the window' is not supported: every checkout PlaceOrder span in the sampled traces carries rpc.grpc.status_code 0 with no error tag, checkout's outbound dependency calls all carry rpc_grpc_status_code 0, and no ERROR-status span-metric series exists for service_name=checkout. (Rejected on the delivered sample, which is not a complete trace graph.)

Human follow-up (not executed here): obtain a comparable pre-window baseline before classifying any latency as elevated, and confirm whether payment's metadata.google.internal / 169.254.169.254 error spans are expected environment-init noise and why payment's ERROR span-metric series reads 0 while error spans are visible in traces.

gaps: No pre-window baseline exists in this run (all series are limited to the fixed 300s window, offset/@ refused), so 'elevated' latency for checkout (server p95 205.33ms) or for its dependency calls cannot be assessed; only absolute in-window values are known.

Absence of an ERROR-status series for checkout (and for cart, email, product-catalog, shipping) is a missing series, not an observed zero error count; the true checkout error rate in this window is unknown.

Trace evidence is a biased, truncated sample: 221/241 checkout spans, 230/250 payment spans, 260/280 product-catalog spans, 354/374 cart spans and 224/244 currency/shipping/email spans were omitted, and the product-catalog, cart and frontend views report incomplete=true ('backend returned as many traces as requested'), so a complete checkout call graph and any failure rate are unknown.

The query for rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count{rpc_grpc_status_code} on payment, product-catalog, cart, currency, shipping and email returned no_data (status no_data, citable_as_fact false), so client-side dependency latency and status distribution for those services is unknown; the same applies to the absence of rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket series for payment, cart, currency, shipping and email.
No http_server_request_duration_seconds series was returned for checkout or email, so their inbound HTTP/error behaviour is unknown (only cart returned 39.92 requests, p95 20.5ms).

Whether the payment ERROR spans (traces 94cfb05cbd9bfcebe99aa181be06f7d4, 598acd55d2618df635fb377c26678f83) are expected cloud-metadata probe noise, and why their increase is not reflected in the payment STATUS_CODE_ERROR metric series, is unresolved by the supplied evidence.
